ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: National statutory framework composed of: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, Articles 2-4, 8, 14-15, 17-23, 31, 32 and 44; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, approving the implementing regulation, Articles 26-29 (identification and verification of ultimate beneficial owners); Ley 6/2023, de 17 de marzo, de los Mercados de Valores y de los Servicios de Inversión, transitional UBO transparency amendments; Real Decreto 162/2023, de 7 de marzo, creating and regulating the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBC); Orden JUS/319/2018, de 21 de marzo, approving the beneficial-owner declaration forms; together with the EU transposition instruments, Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD4/AMLD5), and the interpretative guidance issued by SEPBLAC and the Bank of Spain.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (the RUBC database is accessible only to supervisory authorities, SEPBLAC, tax authorities, and obliged subjects with a verifiable legitimate interest; not publicly searchable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized general power of attorney (Poder Notarial) granted by each non-resident shareholder to the incorporating lawyer, enabling execution of the public deed of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the shareholder's country of residence, with Hague Apostille affixed by the competent national apostille authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for origin jurisdictions not party to the 1961 Hague Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing (Certificado de Vigencia / official registry excerpt) of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passports of all directors, legal representatives and ultimate beneficial owners, together with notarized proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the UBO's jurisdiction of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn translation into Spanish (Traducción Jurada) of all foreign-language public instruments, performed by an officially appointed sworn translator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator (Traductor Jurado) appointed under the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified translation annexed to the notarial protocol; translator's signature and seal verified by the Spanish notary; no separate apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified statement of beneficial ownership and source of funds (Declaración de Titular Real) executed before the Spanish notary at incorporation for filing in the RUBC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish Notary acting within the incorporation protocol
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Document certified within the public deed of incorporation and transmitted electronically by the notary to the Registro Mercantil / RUBC database; consular path not applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of every shareholder, director, legal representative and ultimate beneficial owner against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, including Council Regulation (EU) No. 269/2014 (territorial integrity listing) and Regulation (EU) 2020/1998 (global human rights sanctions); (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (iii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list and the OFAC Sectoral Sanctions Identifications list; and (iv) the Spanish Banco de España and SEPBLAC domestic references on politically exposed persons. PEP status is determined in accordance with Article 14 of Ley 10/2010, including family members and close associates; any PEP identification, negative media indicator, or FATF high-risk jurisdiction referral automatically triggers enhanced due diligence with a written justification archived in the AML/UBO file. Negative screening must be refreshed within 7 calendar days before the notarial deed is executed, and all screening records are retained for a minimum of 5 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) — official electronic name clearance service via the Sede Electrónica at https://www.rmercantil.es and the Registradores de España e-platform at https://www.registradores.org
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Articles 406-410 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010) and RMC operating regulations, the company name must be written in Latin-script characters; names in Spanish or any foreign language are admissible only when transliterated into Latin letters, without ideograms, non-Latin scripts, or unusual diacritical constructions. The RMC performs phonetic and near-character similarity checks, not merely exact-match checks, and normalizes accents. The denomination must not be identical or confusingly similar to any pre-existing registered name, must not mislead as to the corporate type (the embedded tokens 'S.L.', 'S.A.', 'Ltd.' or similar are prohibited), must not infringe prior registered trademarks, and must not be contrary to law, public order, or accepted moral standards.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate issued by the Registro Mercantil Central is valid for 90 days from the date of issuance and is non-extendable; if incorporation has not occurred within the window, counsel must file a fresh name request through the RMC e-portal. Where the RMC issues a certificate of coincidence (an identical or phonetically identical existing denomination), there is no administrative appeal against the coincidence finding; the applicant requests an alternative denomination. Where the name is refused because it contains a prohibited or sensitive token, the applicant must obtain the relevant prior ministerial or state authorization (Bank of Spain for 'Banco'; DGSJFP for 'Nacional', 'Oficial', 'España' terms) and resubmit. Any final administrative refusal or blocking decision of the DGSJFP may be challenged by a recurso de alzada filed with the DGSJFP itself within one month of notification, and, if dismissed, by a subsequent judicial action before the Spanish administrative courts (Jurisdicción Contencioso-Administrativa).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, post-office box, or mail-forwarding address is not acceptable as the sole statutory registered office for an SL. Article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital requires the registered office to coincide with the place of actual management or principal establishment. For this low-risk fast-fashion e-commerce SL, a managed serviced office with a physical address, active lease, and administrative staff is admissible and constitutes the market-standard commercial substance arrangement. The corporate domiciliation provider must deliver a 12-month occupancy letter, which is exhibited to the notary during incorporation; if only a mail-forward address is declared, the Registro Mercantil will refuse inscription and the tax authorities may treat the company as resident outside Spain.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), the Social Security Inspectorate, or the Registro Mercantil authorities in the first operational year for a standard low-risk e-commerce SL. The probability rises to 30-35% where the registered office appears on publicly available data as a shared serviced address, or where annual distance-selling turnover exceeds EUR 100,000 without corresponding physical logistics evidence. AML/CFT registration with the RUBC increases documentary supervision rather than physical inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RMC tariff per name request (approx. EUR 6-11 per denomination, aggregated)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fee for public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) with standard bylaws, SL corporate designation, registered-office exhibition, and RUBC beneficial-owner declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Notary (Notaría de Madrid or province of the registered seat)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial arancel; prevailing market benchmark EUR 450-700 plus VAT for a standard capital-company deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provincial Commercial Registry filing and inscription fee (inscripción de la Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada in the Registro Mercantil Provincial)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (province of the registered office)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registrar tariff computed from the stated share capital and number of deeds

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille management for foreign public instruments (power of attorney, certificate of good standing, UBO passport and address proof) — set of 3 documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille-issuing authority in the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille fees of the origin jurisdiction (average USD 10-20 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation into Spanish (traducción jurada) of non-resident shareholder and director documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (traductor jurado) appointed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs through DGSJFP
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark USD 30-60 per page; estimated 4-6 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal professional fee — pre-incorporation AML/UBO background screening (EU/UN/OFAC/PEP), drafting of bylaws and incorporation minutes, RUBC UBO declaration instruction, NIF provisional application (Modelo 036), and corporate risk memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing fixed-fee market benchmark for a standard SL e-commerce incorporation with due diligence bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Serviced-office physical registered seat — 12-month availability letter and domiciliation set-up exhibited before the notary in support of commercial substance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Serviced office / corporate domiciliation provider (Madrid or Barcelona)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark monthly fee plus one-time administration charge for the occupancy letter

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Spanish Capital Companies Act) — Articles 9 (registered office), 19-23 (formation deed and registration), 52 (participaciones), 62 (minimum capital of €3,000), 210-232 (administration bodies), and Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Regulation of the Commercial Registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry, name certification) and Registro Mercantil Provincial de Madrid (Provincial Commercial Registry, incorporation registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) filed as the first copy with the Registro Mercantil Provincial
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SL minimum subscribed and fully paid-up capital is €3,000 (Article 62 LSC). The capital must be deposited before deed execution in a blocked escrow account held by a Spanish credit institution in the name of the future company; the deposit certificate is released only after registration, liquidation, or with notary authorization for reimbursement. Participaciones (quotas) may not be represented by shares or securities.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The founding members, acting as subscribers, unanimously resolve: (1) To approve the subscription and full payment of €3,000.00, the statutory minimum capital of the SL, represented by one hundred equal participations, the bank certificate being annexed; (2) To adopt the registered office at Calle Gran Vía 28, Madrid, Spain; (3) To appoint [Name Surname] as Administrador Único for an indefinite term; (4) To authorize the director to execute the public deed of incorporation, to request the provisional NIF, to file Modelo 600, and to complete registration with the Registro Mercantil and the Agencia Tributaria; (5) To approve opening corporate bank accounts and adopting Shopify Payments as the primary payment gateway. Passed unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation (Certificación Negativa de Denominación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central — online portal www.rmc.es
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic name certification application through the RMC online platform, listing up to three proposed corporate names in order of preference. The Registrar verifies that the requested denomination is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity. Upon approval, the negative name certificate is issued with a validity of three months.
required_dossiers: Completed application form (Solicitud de Certificación de Denominación Social)
Copy of applicant's NIF/NIE or passport
List of up to three alternative proposed names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused or coincides with a registered one, the applicant may either accept an alternative name already listed, or file a new application with a revised candidate list; in contested cases an appeal may be filed under Article 332 of the Commercial Registry Regulation within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Minimum Capital Deposit and Escrow Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (e.g., Banco Santander S.A., BBVA, or CaixaBank corporate banking desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional escrow account in the name of the future company, deposit the statutory minimum capital of €3,000 by wire transfer, and obtain a blocking certificate (certificado de depósito) issued by bank officers. The certificate must verify the balance is fully available and reserved exclusively for the incorporation until the notarial deed is executed.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate (original or certified copy)
Passports/NIE cards of all founding members
Bank KYC/AML forms including source-of-funds declarations (SOFISA)
Proof of capital transfer and deposit receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank escalates AML/KYC queries, provide the requested documentation within five business days; if the chosen institution declines the file, open an escrow account at another Spanish credit institution and re-deposit the capital while preserving the name reservation priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary within the Ilustre Colegio Notarial de Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding members must appear personally or by legal representative before the notary, who will read and authenticate the deed of incorporation, the bylaws (estatutos), the corporate object covering e-commerce retail of fast-fashion apparel and footwear, the registered office, the share structure, and the designation of the sole director. The notary issues authorized first and certified copies for subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Negative name certificate (valid for three months)
Bank certificate of minimum capital deposit
Passports and NIE cards of all founders
Draft bylaws (estatutos sociales) consistent with LSC requirements
First Board Resolution minutes (if adopted prior to the deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary finds statutory defects or incomplete clauses, the founders may execute a supplementary correction at the same or a subsequent notarial sitting within twenty business days; otherwise a new deed must be executed reflecting the corrected bylaws.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — provincial tax office via Form 036 (Declaración Censal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 036 together with the first copy of the notarial deed and an explanatory letter requesting the provisional NIF. AEAT issues the provisional tax identification number on the same day or within one business day, which is valid until the definitive NIF is granted after Commercial Registry registration.
required_dossiers: Modelo 036 (census declaration) signed by the director
First copy or due copy of the notarial deed
Director's identification document
Application letter requesting provisional NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT detects inconsistent census data, submit a corrective Form 036/037 within ten days; if the deed is not yet registered, the notary's filing receipt may be presented as documentary support to obtain the provisional NIF.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Transfer Tax and Stamp Duty (Impuesto de Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados, AJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Consejería de Economía, Hacienda y Empleo — Comunidad de Madrid (Modelo 600 electronic filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Modelo 600 electronically within thirty calendar days after the deed execution, applying the Madrid regional AJD rate of 0.75% on the capital of €3,000 (€22.50). Upload the public deed and the self-assessed declaration, and obtain the payment receipt for submission to the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: First or certified copy of the notarial deed
Modelo 600 self-assessment declaration
Company provisional NIF
Bank transfer or payment confirmation of the AJD amount
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the self-assessment is rejected or payment is late, the surcharge regime under the Ley General Tributaria applies; the taxpayer should pay the principal and the corresponding recargo (surcharge) within three months of notification and may submit a rectification request (solicitud de rectificación) when the taxable basis is contested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Registration and Definitive NIF Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil de Madrid (Provincial) and Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first copy of the notarial deed with the Registro Mercantil de Madrid within five business days of execution. The Registrar reviews legality, lists the company, and issues the registration certificate. Upon presentation of the registration certificate to AEAT via Form 036, the definitive NIF/CIF is granted, completing the legal formation.
required_dossiers: First copy of the notarial deed
Proof of AJD payment (Modelo 600 receipt)
Modelo 036 provisional NIF application
Registration certificate (certificación registral) issued by the Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a defect notice (defecto subsanable), the directors must cure within the granted period of fifteen to thirty days by executing a rectification deed before the notary; if the defect is held insubsanable, the formation procedure restarts with a new name reservation and a new deed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no manufacturing or industrial activity; pure electronic retail of fast-fashion apparel (ISIC 4791) requires no industrial operating license
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial license required; a municipal 'Licencia de Apertura' (opening license) applies only if the company operates physical customer-facing premises or staffed warehouses subject to local urban planning rules

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) / Agencia de Protección Ambiental de la Comunidad de Madrid
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — online apparel retail does not constitute an IPPC industrial installation and requires no EIA report or environmental registration under Ley 21/2013
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for industrial emissions; obligations limited to packaging waste and extended producer responsibility under Ley 7/2022 (residuos y suelos contaminados) and RAEE rules in Real Decreto 110/2015 if handling electronics returns

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational risk prevention plan under Ley 31/1995 (PRL) mandatory for any staffed office or warehouse; municipal fire safety certification and structural load inspection required for premises if physical warehousing is established; GDPR data processing register obligations supervised by the Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD) for customer personal data processed at registered offices.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); online portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident entity applies to AEAT (Modelo 036/030) for a Spanish tax-identification number (NIF-IVA for VAT and NIF for corporate tax), appointing a tax representative in Spain and submitting notarized incorporation documents, power of attorney, and a certificate of foreign tax residence. Registration is mandatory before the first taxable transaction; no minimum capital is required for the SL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada taxed as an opaque corporation under Corporate Income Tax: standard 25%; 15% reduced rate for newly created entities in the first two taxable periods with positive tax base; national territorial scope; Canary Islands ZEC preferential regime available).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election; statutory elections include the ETVE foreign-securities holding regime, consolidated tax group regime (art. 64 LIS) at 25%, new-entity reduced-rate election, R&D and investment tax-credit elections, and ATAD 2 hybrid-mismatch alignment rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold: registration (Modelo 036) is mandatory before the first taxable transaction. Intra-EU distance-selling Union threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year; the simplified VAT regime applies only to individuals with prior-year turnover under EUR 250,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time fiscal clearance: mandatory e-invoicing under Ley Crea y Crece for B2B/R2R (deadlines pending implementing order); SII (Immediate Supply of Information) real-time/periodic VAT-book filing for large enterprises; Veri*factu (RD 1007/2023) requires issuance systems guaranteeing invoice authenticity and integrity via QR codes and electronic signatures.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT (exemption with right to deduction) on exports of goods to non-EU destinations under art. 21 LIVA, and on intra-EU dispatches under art. 25 LIVA where the customer's valid VAT ID and the supplier's EC Sales List are held; services directly related to exported goods, and certain offshore services under arts. 69-70 LIVA, are zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank proof of export payment)
AEAT-validated proof of exit from the EU
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Failure to substantiate export within statutory periods triggers retrospective VAT assessment plus late-payment interest; penalties under arts. 191-194 LGT range from 50% to 150% of the amount, with aggravated 100%-150% rates for concealment; fraudulent export zero-rating claims exceeding EUR 120,000 are prosecutable as tax fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) and the Spanish Directorate General for International Trade and Investments (Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones, DGCIIN) under the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a Eurozone member; the Euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. No exchange controls exist for profit remittances, dividends, or capital repatriation, subject to compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) and tax reporting obligations. Current account transactions (e.g., trade payments, service fees) are unrestricted. Capital account operations (e.g., foreign direct investment, loans) require statistical declaration to the Bank of Spain for balance-of-payments purposes, but no prior authorization is needed for EU residents. Non-EU investors may need to file post-investment declarations if the investment exceeds certain thresholds (e.g., €3 million or 10% of share capital). Profit remittance is subject to standard corporate income tax (25%) and withholding tax on dividends (19% for EU residents, 19% for non-EU unless treaty relief applies).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign currency in bank accounts, either domestically or abroad, subject to reporting requirements for balance-of-payments statistics. The statutory timeline for reporting export transactions is monthly via the Bank of Spain's statistical declaration system (e.g., Form C-1 for transactions above €50,000). There is no requirement to convert export receipts into EUR within a specific period; however, for tax purposes, foreign currency income must be converted to EUR at the official exchange rate on the transaction date. No minimum conversion ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (current account for daily transactions) and Capital Escrow Account (for initial share capital deposit if required by notary)
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for operational accounts, but Medium for capital escrow due to regulatory constraints. Spanish law permits the use of Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions (PIs) licensed in the EU (e.g., Wise, Revolut, N26) for business accounts, provided they hold a valid passporting license under the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2). However, for the initial capital deposit required to incorporate an SL (minimum €3,000), the bank must issue a certificate of deposit; most EMIs do not offer this service. For ongoing operations, EMIs are viable for cross-border payments, multi-currency accounts, and FX conversion, but they may not provide full treasury services (e.g., trade finance, LC issuance). Legal constraints: EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot offer lending or certain escrow services. Additionally, some Spanish tax authorities may require a domestic bank account for VAT refunds or certain government interactions. Overall, a hybrid approach (traditional bank for escrow and primary operational account, plus an EMI for cross-border efficiency) is recommended.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial onboarding of a corporate entity. Directors (or a legal representative with a power of attorney) must appear in person at the bank branch to sign the account opening agreement and complete the KYC interview. Remote onboarding is possible for existing clients or via video identification for individuals, but for corporate entities, most Spanish banks require a physical visit, especially for non-resident directors. Some banks (e.g., BBVA, Santander) offer digital onboarding for SLs with a Spanish tax ID (NIF) and a local registered address, but they may still require a notarized power of attorney and apostilled documents. For non-resident directors, a local representative (e.g., a Spanish resident with a valid NIF) may be appointed to handle the interview, but the bank may still require the director to appear at least once. The mandate is strict for capital escrow accounts due to the need to certify the deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: If the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is not clearly identified or is a nominee, the bank will flag the account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a corporate structure chart, certified copies of the register of ultimate beneficial owners (from the Spanish Commercial Registry), and a declaration of UBO per Spanish AML law (Ley 10/2010). Include notarized and apostilled identification documents (passport) for all UBOs holding >25% shares or control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure: If any shareholder, director, or counterparty is from a FATF blacklist or high-risk third country (e.g., Iran, North Korea, Syria), the bank will reject or escalate.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed source of funds and source of wealth statement, with supporting bank statements, tax returns, and commercial contracts. Obtain a legal opinion from a Spanish attorney confirming the legitimacy of the funds and the absence of sanctions exposure. If the jurisdiction is on the EU list of non-cooperative jurisdictions, consider restructuring ownership to avoid the trigger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns: High-volume cash deposits, rapid in-and-out transfers, or transactions inconsistent with the declared business model (e.g., fast-fashion e-commerce) may trigger enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a comprehensive business plan, sales contracts, supplier invoices, and logistics documentation. Provide a forecast of expected transaction volumes and values. Implement robust transaction monitoring and maintain a clear audit trail. If the bank requests, provide a sworn statement of the business purpose and a copy of the e-commerce platform agreement (e.g., Shopify, Klarna).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete corporate documentation: Missing or expired certificates, lack of apostille, or non-translated documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a full corporate kit: Certificate of Incorporation, Articles of Association (Estatutos), NIF (Tax ID) certificate, and a certificate of the registered office. All documents must be translated into Spanish by a certified translator and apostilled if issued outside Spain. Ensure the power of attorney (if any) is notarized and apostilled.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: For initial share capital injection (minimum €3,000) from a non-resident shareholder, the transfer must be made via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the SL's capital escrow account in Spain. The purpose code must be 'S001' (Investment in shares) or 'S002' (Capital contribution) as per the Bank of Spain's Balance of Payments classification. The transfer must include the SL's NIF and the shareholder's identification. For subsequent capital injections (e.g., loans or additional equity), use purpose code 'S003' (Loans) or 'S004' (Other investments). Verification: The bank will require a copy of the notarized deed of incorporation and the shareholder resolution approving the injection. For loans, a loan agreement must be filed with the Bank of Spain if the amount exceeds €1 million. All inbound transfers are subject to AML checks; the bank may request source of funds documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: For payments to suppliers (e.g., garment manufacturers in Asia), the primary rail is SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers. For larger or recurring transactions, a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) may be used, typically issued by the SL's bank in favor of the supplier's bank. The LC can be confirmed or unconfirmed, with payment terms (e.g., at sight or deferred). For e-commerce refunds to customers, use the payment gateway (e.g., Shopify Payments) which settles via card networks (Visa, Mastercard) or local schemes (e.g., Bizum). For cross-border disbursements to contractors or service providers, use SWIFT MT103 with appropriate purpose codes (e.g., 'S200' for services). The bank may require supporting invoices and contracts for each transaction to comply with AML and tax reporting. For high-volume, low-value payments, consider using an EMI (e.g., Wise) for cost-effective FX conversion, but ensure the EMI is licensed and the transactions are reported.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards: Over-the-counter (OTC) contracts with a bank to lock in an exchange rate for a future date, typically up to 12 months. Permissible for hedging commercial exposures (e.g., USD or GBP receivables/payables).

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): Used for currencies with limited convertibility (e.g., CNY, INR) where the settlement is in EUR based on the difference between the contracted rate and the spot rate. Permissible for hedging exposures to emerging market currencies.

Currency Swaps: Exchange of principal and interest payments in different currencies, used for longer-term hedging or to manage liquidity in multiple currencies. Permissible for treasury operations, subject to bank approval and documentation under ISDA agreements.
FX Options: Purchased options (calls/puts) to hedge against adverse FX movements while retaining upside potential. Permissible but may require a higher credit rating or collateral.
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS): For managing both FX and interest rate risk on foreign currency loans or investments. Permissible for sophisticated treasury operations.

stage_5.statutory_deliverable: Name of annual return, corporate declaration, or franchise filing
stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: Financial penalties and timeline triggering administrative strike-off

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General rate 25% under Law 27/2014 (LIS). Newly created Spanish SLs are taxed at 15% for the first two taxable periods with a positive tax base. Small entities with prior-year net turnover below EUR 1,000,000 apply 23% to the first EUR 50,000 of taxable base and 25% above that threshold. Available reliefs include R&D and innovation credits, employment-related deductions, international double-taxation credits, and the patent box regime for qualifying IP income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_time_rule: Unlimited carryforward under Article 26 LIS; annual offset of negative tax bases is capped at 70% of positive taxable base (60% for entities with prior-year net turnover of EUR 20,000,000 or more), with an absolute floor allowing offset of at least EUR 1,000,000 per year regardless of the cap.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed electronically via Sede Electrónica de la Agencia Tributaria; mandatory electronic submission for legal entities.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly advance payment filings (Modelo 202/222) during the year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period; for a calendar-year-end SL, the annual return is due by 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer NIF, corporate name, registered office, principal activity under CNAE 4791 (retail sale via Internet) and tax period start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SL is the resident taxpayer; non-resident shareholders do not complete this return. Their NIF and residence data are captured in Form 210 and in withholding reporting on distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss before tax in accordance with the Spanish General Chart of Accounts (PGC), reflecting all fast-fashion e-commerce revenues, cost of sales, logistics, Shopify and Klarna settlement fees, and returns provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All online revenues attributable to the Spanish permanent establishment must be declared; no imputation of foreign parent revenue is made in this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments reconciling accounting result to taxable base: non-deductible expenses, exempt dividends, depreciation recalculated on tax basis, inventory seasonality provisions, and impairment losses not deductible until recognition criteria are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax base must be computed exclusively on the SL's own operations; intra-group transactions with related entities must be supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Taxable base before NOL offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Positive or negative tax base derived after adjustments, before applying prior-year negative tax base carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If resulting taxable base derives from cross-border related-party transactions, supporting OECD TP documentation must be referenced in consolidating schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of prior negative taxable bases offset under Article 26 LIS; subject to 70%/60% annual cap with EUR 1,000,000 floor.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No time limitation applies; however, records of loss origin, amount and composition must be preserved for the full period of offset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% general statutory rate; 15% for newly created SLs in the first two positive tax periods; 23% reduced scale on the first EUR 50,000 for small entities with turnover below EUR 1,000,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Rate selection must be justified in an annex; abuse of the reduced rate by artificial fragmentation of e-commerce activity is auditable and penalised.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Full tax amount, deductions and credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Result of applying the rate to the taxable base (quota íntegra), reduced by R&D credits, withholding tax credits, double-taxation relief, deductions and bonuses to determine quota líquida.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits for taxes paid abroad on foreign-source income require certification of foreign levy; records must accompany the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refundable after offsetting quarterly advance payments (Modelo 202/222), withholdings suffered and payments on account; payment settled through the AEAT banking gateway.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any distribution made to non-resident shareholders must have had 19% WHT withheld and paid; the WHT is not credited in Modelo 200 of the SL.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission surcharges under Article 27 LGT: 5% if filed within 3 months of the deadline, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% thereafter, plus late-payment interest. Omission of the return triggers Article 198 LGT formal penalties of EUR 200 to EUR 20,000 depending on the data and rebuttal. Inaccurate or incomplete returns triggering under-assessment attract proportional penalties of 50%-150% of the amount evaded under Article 191 LGT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202 (standard quarterly instalment) and Modelo 222 (consolidated/large taxpayer instalment) filed electronically via Sede Electrónica AEAT.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly advance payments for the current fiscal period, filed in April, October and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due 20 April, 20 October and 20 December for calendar-year taxpayers; for non-calendar years, within 20 days following the advance period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, corporate name and tax period of the filing instalment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident SL alone completes this form; non-resident shareholders have no reporting obligation here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection between Article 40.2 LIS (18% of year-to-date positive taxable base) and Article 40.3 LIS (based on prior-year tax liability, used by entities with net turnover exceeding EUR 10,000,000 or other significant-turnover rules).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The chosen modality must be the one that minimises not simply the payment but the risk of underestimation penalties; consistent TP positions must be reflected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C / Instalment base and amount
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the advance payment: 18% of the positive taxable base accrued to the prepayment date, or percentage of the prior-year tax charge, reduced by withholdings and payments already made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cash-flow forecasts from fast-fashion cycles (peak season in Q4) must be matched to the December instalment; artificial deferral is sanctionable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-filing or underpayment of quarterly instalments: late-payment surcharge of 20% plus annual late-payment interest; if the instalment is not filed at all, Article 191 LGT penalty of 50%-150% of the unpaid amount, in addition to coercive collection measures.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on gross dividends distributed to a non-resident beneficial owner under Article 25.1 of the Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax Code (TRLIRNR), unless an exemption or reduced treaty rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced or zero rate, the non-resident shareholder must submit, prior to or at distribution, a valid certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the residence state's tax authority and a beneficial-ownership statement. For the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, a minimum 10% shareholding held for at least one year and absence of an abuse/hybrid mismatch must be evidenced. The AEAT operates a prior accreditation procedure for reduced withholding; where excess tax is withheld, the non-resident may file Form 210 to request a refund within the four-year limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties sourced to Spain: 24% statutory; interest: 19% statutory. Under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, qualifying associated companies resident in the EU are exempt at source. Treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 10%, conditional on TRC, beneficial ownership and anti-abuse provisions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Local File must be prepared where the aggregate value of related-party transactions with one related entity exceeds EUR 250,000; Master File is mandatory when the group's consolidated net turnover exceeds EUR 45,000,000; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenues of at least EUR 750,000,000. Even below local-file thresholds, the arm's-length principle under Article 18 LIS applies and the SL must be able to evidence compliance.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but substantive economic activity is mandatory under the Spanish GAAR in Article 15.1 LIS, the CFC regime in Article 100 LIS, ATAD and OECD BEPS Action 6. A Spanish SL without local management, employees, premises and operational functions, or interposed exclusively to obtain Spanish tax treaty benefits, will be recharacterised as an artificial arrangement and denied treaty/regime relief.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully understating fast-fashion online revenues from Shopify Payments, Klarna BNPL transactions, PayPal and bank settlement rails; issuing no invoices on a substantial volume of sales; or routing proceeds to non-declared foreign accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal offence under Article 305 of the Criminal Code (CP): imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded where the evaded tax exceeds EUR 120,000. Administrative re-assessment includes late-payment interest, a 20% surcharge and penalties of 50%-150% of the tax amount under LGT Article 191. All tax incentives are forfeited.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: De jure and de facto directors are jointly and severally liable under LGT Articles 42 and 43 for unpaid corporation tax where criminal evasion or gross negligence is proven; courts apply piercing of the corporate veil; convicted directors face imprisonment, asset attachment, travel bans and disqualification from managing Spanish companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Spanish SL as a letter-box vehicle with no local office, staff, management or business purpose, interposed in intra-group digital retail flows solely to obtain the Spanish 15%-25% tax rate and EU or DTA benefits; channelling profits through offshore no-tax sister companies with no economic activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation and disregard of the artificial arrangement under Article 15.1 LIS; CFC income attribution under Article 100 LIS; denial of treaty benefits under BEPS Action 6; 50%-150% penalty on the re-assessed tax; potential nullity of corporate acts if fraud is proven under Articles 6-8 of the Spanish Civil Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors participating in the shell structure are jointly liable for the full tax debt, including penalties; judicial veil-piercing is available under Spanish case law; directors may be indicted for fraudulent insolvency, false accounting and tax evasion, with custodial sentences and travel prohibition pending trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / BNPL and Payment-Rails Compliance Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating Klarna BNPL and Shopify Payments with deficient KYC-CDD onboarding, no PEP screening, absence of STR (Suspicious Transaction Report) filing with SEPBLAC, or knowingly accepting layered settlement flows inconsistent with declared turnover and inventory capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 10/2010 on prevention of money laundering: grave infringement fines of EUR 60,001 to EUR 5,000,000; publication of the sanction; prohibition of the entity from continuing as a payment aggregation beneficiary; confiscation or freezing of funds where laundering is established; criminal money-laundering liability under CP Article 301.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the reporting SL face personal fines for failure to appoint a compliance officer and for gross AML negligence; if wilful conduct is shown, imprisonment under Article 301 CP, individual fines, asset seizure and travel bans apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting related-party transactions above EUR 250,000 without a Local File; paying non-arm's-length management fees to a foreign fast-fashion IP-licensing affiliate in a low-tax jurisdiction; granting interest-free shareholder loans; or refusing the AEAT TP documentation request during inspection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's-length adjustment under Article 18 LIS; proportional penalty of 50% of the resulting tax under-assessment under Article 191 LGT plus 20% surcharge and late interest; non-documentation penalties under Article 18.10 LIS; disallowance of deductible expense where documentation is missing or fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause the filing of a materially inaccurate return may be held jointly and severally liable under LGT Article 43; willful TP manipulation constitutes criminal tax evasion exposure under CP Article 305, with personal fines, imprisonment and restitution obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Resident Equity Lane / UBO Reporting Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SL's share capital is held through a holding entity in a zero-tax jurisdiction whose ultimate beneficial owner is not declared to Spain's Beneficial Ownership Registry; distributing dividends to non-resident shareholders without applying or reporting the 19% WHT and without obtaining TRC-backed relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: UBO registry infringements under Law 10/2010 attract fines of up to EUR 60,000 and publication; failure to withhold and pay the 19% WHT triggers LGT penalties of 50%-150% of the under-withheld amount; unrelieved distributions may be recharacterised as constructive dividends with additional 25% corporate tax penalty exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the unremitted withholding tax under LGT Article 41, civil restitution; false UBO statements can support criminal money-laundering or false-document charges, leading to imprisonment, travel bans and disqualification from corporate office.
